〈비트코인이 약세인 eu〉

items.summary:
〈비트코인이 약세인 eu〉

1. 비트코인 채굴사들이 AI 데이터센터 사업으로 전환하고 있음. 기존 채굴보다 AI 인프라가 더 유망하다고 판단한 것.

2. 그런데 AI 사업에는 막대한 선행투자가 필요함. 여기에 AI 버블 논란과 데이터센터 건설 반대까지 겹치며 불확실성이 커짐.

3. 결국 채굴사들이 BTC를 대거 현금화하기 시작함. MARA와 Riot이 올해 매각한 물량만 약 6만 BTC에 달함.

4. 주요 AI 전환 채굴사들이 아직 보유한 BTC도 약 4.4만 개로 추산됨. 거래소 전체 보유량 약 345만 개의 1.3% 수준임.

5. 반면 BTC를 대규모로 사들이던 스트래티지 등 DAT들은 프리미엄이 약해지며 매수 여력이 줄어들고 있음. 스트래티지의 최근 4주 매수량은 고작 2,332 BTC.

6. 거시경제도 좋지 않음. 앤트로픽 IPO에만 810억 달러가 몰리는 등 자금이 AI로 집중되고, 미국 국채금리 상승과 추가 금리 인상 우려까지 겹침.

7. 다행히 유가는 조금 내려왔지만 이란 전쟁은 여전히 진행 중임. 전력을 소비해야만 하는 PoW 채굴에는 에너지 가격의 불확실성도 부담임.

8. BTC 가격 하락 → 채굴 수익성 악화 → BTC 현금화 압력 증가. 반면 DAT의 매수 여력은 약해지는 악순환도 우려됨.

9. 여기에 장기적으로는 양자컴퓨터와 AI 시대의 보안 위협까지 대응해야 함. 특히 양자 위협에 대응하려면 네트워크 차원의 합의와 업그레이드가 필요함.

10. 더 근본적으로는 반감기로 채굴 보상이 계속 감소하는데, 언젠가 거래 수수료만으로 충분한 네트워크 보안을 유지할 수 있느냐는 문제도 남아 있음.

11. 그냥 지금은 비트코인에 ㅈ같은 악재밖에 없는 것 같음. 오히려 이 정도면 가격이 잘 버티고 있다는 생각이 들 정도.

12. 그런데 생각해 보면 이 중 상당수가 PoW의 경제적 구조와 연결되어 있음.

13. PoS는 스테이킹 보상으로 공급량이 늘어난다는 이유로 비판받곤 함. 하지만 그 역시 네트워크 보안을 유지하기 위한 비용임.

14. 그렇다면 PoW는 어떨까? 반감기로 채굴 보상은 계속 감소하는데, 막대한 전력과 자본을 투입하는 채굴자들에게 장기적으로 충분한 보상을 제공할 수 있을까?

15. 결국 PoW든 PoS든 보안을 유지하기 위한 비용을 누군가는 부담해야 함. 중요한 건 어떤 방식이 더 지속가능하고 효율적인가의 문제라고 생각함.

솔직히 요즘은 PoW가 정말 맞는 방향인지 모르겠음.

비트코인이 지금까지 성공적으로 작동해 왔다는 사실과 별개로, 앞으로 수십 년 동안에도 PoW가 최선의 합의 방식일지는 의문임.

나는 여전히 장기적인 지속가능성과 자본 효율성 측면에서 PoS가 더 합리적인 방향이라고 생각함.

이렇게 쓰면 개 욕처먹을거 같은데
그냥 요즘은 그 생각이 더 강해지고 있음.
반박 대환영.

items.title: Should I be concerned? Please follow this chain and tell me if I need to be frea
items.summary:
Should I be concerned? Please follow this chain and tell me if I need to be freaking out and blocking everything down or what:

Last week, Person A mentioned Person B with first and last name to me in an iMessage and included a link to B’s LinkedIn. B has a somewhat common first and last name. 

I have clicked on this LinkedIn link several times since. 

A then introduced me to B via TG. After a few short messages B and I scheduled a meeting and B sent me a calendar invite to my work email address. 

Now, a few days later, I just received a spam email to my *personal* email address where the “from” field had B’s first and last name but the sender was a random email address. This was NOT a platform that I had ever discussed B on, and B doesn’t have this email address, and I have never emailed anyone with that name from this email. 

How did the scammer know that I had recently talked with or about B and that their name would be front of mind to use it for their scam email? Is it just random chance that they happened to use this name since B’s first and last name are kind of common? 

Or should I be concerned someone has been watching my devices or has access to my work email, TG, LI, or iMessage??? 

Or is it something like B got hacked and their friend also got hacked and so the hacker used the friend’s email to email me since I was also a contact?? If so, how did they get my personal email the than the TG or work email?

I’m freaked out about this but am not sure if it’s that I’m comprised or someone else is or if it’s just a random coincidence 😰

cc @tayvano_ @PabloSabbatella

items.title:
Can AI help Ethereum EIP editors manage 550+ open PRs? 

That was one of the int
items.summary:
Can AI help Ethereum EIP editors manage 550+ open PRs? 

That was one of the interesting discussions at today’s EIPIP meeting. 

A few highlights:

- @JochemBrouwer96 shared AGENTS.md: 
 AI-assisted reviews will be piloted. Comments only, no auto-merging. Human oversight stays.
https://t.co/lxQP4R2HTn

- @EIPsInsight demoed EIP Builder showcasing support to authors & editors to draft, validate & review proposals.
https://t.co/jXacRil6cv
Editors discussed potential integration with https://t.co/FOwGnx8qyw.

- Exceptional PR merging (Glamsterdam EIPs): 
Editors reaffirmed that PRs require author approval, even for factual corrections.

- EIP Coordinator: CfI will be closed in favor.
PR to update EIP-1 with the Coordinator role/name looks good and can be merged. 
https://t.co/bX96HtFUxI

- Keeper of Consensus: Election remains open for 30 days. CfI will be updated to reflect the voting window.
https://t.co/IZLV1eMiDa

- PR backlog: EIP Editors encouraged to join Office Hours to help move reviews forward.

AI can help us scale EIP reviews, but human oversight, author ownership and process neutrality must remain at the center.

Next EIPIP: Dec 16.

items.title:
New post on Eth Research!

Encrypted Account: a PIN that lives in the contract
items.summary:
New post on Eth Research!

Encrypted Account: a PIN that lives in the contract

By:
- Himess

🔗 https://t.co/szcAfQ4gUs

Highlights:
- The design is an ERC-4337 smart account that stores a PIN-derived fingerprint on-chain as a ciphertext and verifies guesses using threshold FHE, so no server ever holds the PIN or enforces rate limits.
- Its core trick is “count first, reveal after”: the contract increments an on-chain wrong-guess score before the (encrypted) success bit is allowed to be decrypted, preventing offline brute force and limiting online attempts (simulated to ~12 guesses per 30 days under default rules).
- A stolen signing key is deliberately low-power: it can only send to pre-approved addresses within per-asset daily limits; new recipients, large amounts, approvals, or arbitrary calls require the PIN plus a time delay (e.g., 1 hour / 48 hours by default).
- Wrong PIN attempts can be made economically painful via an external ETH bond that doubles with each miss; incorrect guesses forfeit the bond into the account, meaning a thief with only the key pays the owner for failed guessing.
- There is a non-FHE “escape hatch”: the key alone can start an emergency sweep to a pre-consented address after a long delay (e.g., 30 days), which still works even if the FHE/threshold network is unavailable; the whole system is a testnet-only, unaudited research prototype on Sepolia under MIT license.

ELI5:
Imagine your crypto wallet has a secret PIN, but instead of a company server checking it, the wallet’s smart contract checks it by itself. The PIN is stored in a locked, scrambled form (encrypted) so nobody can read it, and the contract can still compare your PIN guess to the real one. Each time someone guesses, the contract counts the guess first and only then allows the network to reveal whether it was right—so attackers can’t download the data and try millions of PINs offline. If someone steals your key, they can only do small “allowed” payments; anything risky needs the PIN plus a waiting period, and wrong PIN guesses cost the attacker money that goes into your account. There’s also an emergency “escape” that can move funds to a pre-chosen safe address after a delay, even if the encryption network is down.

items.title:
New EIP!

Dynamic individual consolidation incentive

🔗 https://t.co/hYIZq38vVt
items.summary:
New EIP!

Dynamic individual consolidation incentive

🔗 https://t.co/hYIZq38vVt

Highlights:
- Introduces a new BeaconState field, `consolidation_force`, and an epoch-processing step that subtracts a consolidation incentive from every active validator’s balance after rewards/penalties are processed.
- Defines a validator-count target schedule that linearly ramps from `VALIDATOR_TARGET_START` to `VALIDATOR_TARGET_END` over ~1.5 years (example), then stays at the terminal target; the mechanism reacts to how far actual validator count is above/below this target.
- Uses an integral-controller-like force: it rises while validator count is above target (slowly, e.g., 300-day time constant) and falls when below target (10× faster, e.g., 30-day time constant), capped between 0% and 100%.
- The per-validator subtraction is proportional to the validator’s full attestation reward and scaled by effective balance so that a 32 ETH validator pays the most, and a 2048 ETH validator pays zero—making the private cost roughly per *validator seat* rather than per ETH staked.
- To avoid over-penalizing validators already committed to merge, the validator-count metric excludes active validators that are sources of pending consolidations (though they still pay the incentive until they actually exit), improving stability during consolidation-queue backlogs.

ELI5:
Ethereum has way too many “validator accounts,” and each one adds work for the network in every finality round. This proposal sets a moving goal for how many validators there should be, gradually lowering the goal over time. If there are more validators than the goal, the protocol slowly turns up a “pressure knob” and, every epoch, takes a small amount of ETH from each validator—taking the most from small (32 ETH) validators and nothing from fully consolidated (2048 ETH) validators. That makes it personally costly to keep lots of small validators, encouraging people to merge them into fewer, bigger validators until the count comes back down.

items.title:
New post on Eth Research!

Reveal a key, not a payload: sending the ePBS payload
items.summary:
New post on Eth Research!

Reveal a key, not a payload: sending the ePBS payload before the reveal

By:
- cskiraly

🔗 https://t.co/dbNSzdm2rf

Highlights:
- In baseline Gloas, payload propagation starts only after the builder reveals it; builders often delay revealing (to avoid leaking contents if the block is dropped, and to handle equivocation/timing issues), which eats into the payload’s dissemination window.
- “Pre-seeding” changes the flow: after a bid is included in a valid beacon block, the builder broadcasts erasure-coded encrypted payload chunks immediately, then at reveal time broadcasts only a 32-byte decryption key (plus signature), letting the network decrypt once enough chunks are present.
- The main benefit is time: encrypted payload transfer can start at block arrival rather than reveal time, potentially saving up to ~3 seconds in a 12-second slot when blocks arrive early (less benefit for late blocks or earlier reveals).
- Protocol-level adjustments are needed: bids must commit to the ciphertext chunk root and a hash of the key; nodes should only forward ciphertext chunks once the corresponding bid is included; PTC “payload present” voting becomes contingent on receiving the key plus enough chunks and successful decryption/checks before the deadline.
- The main cost/tradeoff is increased builder optionality: if only a key remains to be sent, the builder can decide later whether to reveal (withhold the key) while still keeping payload contents private; this can increase the value/use of the builder’s “free option,” and also wastes network bandwidth if ciphertext was widely propagated but the key is withheld.

ELI5:
In Ethereum’s proposed ePBS/Gloas design, the “builder” waits to send the block’s big contents (the payload) until they’re sure the block won’t get discarded. That waiting time steals from the limited time the payload has to reach everyone. The idea here is: send the payload early but locked in a box (encrypted) right after the block includes the builder’s bid, and later reveal only the tiny “unlock code” (a short key). That way, the heavy data can spread while the builder is waiting, and the final reveal is just a small message.

items.summary:
I think this would be terribly bearish $ETH and I thought the point of saying the L2 roadmap hasn't worked out and getting back to scaling mainnet is to . . . not do this? 

To focus exclusively or mainly on the 'bulletin board' vision would be taking Ethereum back to being a pre-pmf startup basically as there is no proven material market for zk-notarization service where other applications prove they haven't done fraud 

I'm fine that Ethereum is good at doing this and will make it part of its market, but it's a very early-stage market. Currently it is only "L2s" but even most of them are using this on a 'trial basis' so to speak as they are not Stage 2. 

We can't abandon the goal of having a thriving, stateful execution environment for DeFi on Ethereum mainnet, where ETH is the premium programmable SoV

items.summary:
They say if you want to get rich quick, buy the things that rich people will want before they want it. 

There is a clear emergence of members clubs in wealthy cities. Annabel’s, a famous London club for the elites, opening up in NYC is a clear sign of the times. 

This is likely because everything else has become more accessible to everyone else. Your average elitist is pissed that their favorite hangout spot is less quiet. On top of that, more people than ever can now take tropical vacations, learn things that were previously gatekept to certain social classes. The dude working in the mines was not fluent in French, but his granddaughter now is. With a rising class of “new money” and an increasingly outnumbered class of “old money,” comes an opportunity for the savvy socialite minds that can connect the very “best” of the two. Member clubs and retreats are an obvious manifestation of that connection.

P2P Networking #11 - November 18, 2026

client updates:
- jxs: researching EIP-8411 integration, exploring Waggle app/network interface boundary
- Prysm: beginning EIP-8411 prototype; reviewing Daniel's PR for 1-1 Waggle integration
- Nethermind: P2P improvements in .NET; interested in PQ-related protocols; will review EIP-8411 this week
- Geth (Felix): mempool improvements; working on post-quantum ENR and Discovery v5 transition plan; to post in Discord
- Lodestar (cayman): building new Ethereum-tailored networking stack in Zig; js-libp2p moving to maintenance mode
- Silver (vlad): libp2p-compatible but not libp2p; producing production-ready Rust seacast library
- Ethlambda: beacon client launched, presented in Cambridge; experimenting with PQ signature sizes vs BLS

networking specs:
- Felix demoed unified P2P networking spec repo merging devp2p (EL) and consensus-specs (CL) networking into one place
- Repo introduces legacy/current/experimental versioning; full reified specs per version; EIP-named draft files for in-progress proposals
- CL networking spec compiled to single up-to-date document (v6 at Gloas); fork-based versioning retained; gossip validation functions stay in consensus-specs
- Planned additions: Waggle and seacast under new 'broadcast' directory; QUIC transport spec; libp2p adapter spec
- jxs: drove QUIC adoption but has no plans to deprecate TCP; cayman: QUIC-only vision appealing long-term; Silver is QUIC-only

webtx protocol:
- Geth (Bosul): WebTX — new sub-protocol allowing browsers to submit transactions directly to EL P2P network via WebTransport/QUIC, bypassing RPC
- ENR extended with certificate hash field (QH); two-week rotation with advance announcement; identity proof via signed challenge on session open
- Browser connections limited: 10s lifetime, disconnect after first message, IP-based rate limiting on invalid transactions
- Protocol is write-only (transaction submit + result response); peer exchange planned; onion routing considered long-term
- WebTX merged in Geth; browser→node connections testable on mainnet today; spec PR: ethereum/devp2p#276

xmss signature broadcast simulations:
- Kamil ran gossipsub simulations (~3,700 nodes, 32K validators) for XMSS/large-signature attestation propagation
- Reducing gossipsub mesh degree from 8→4 cuts average duplicates from 4→2.5 with no latency regression

- ProbeLab (Mikel): simulations reflect happy path only; adversarial/churn scenarios (eclipse, delayed forwarding) should be included in roadmap
- cayman: simulations should include EIP-7870 bandwidth-bound nodes; bad numbers justify updating bandwidth assumptions

eip 8411 waggle:
- EIP-8411 is CFI for Hegota; scope may be reconsidered pending upcoming ACDC discussions
- Daniel's PR (EIPs#12671) updates EIP-8411 to use Waggle; Lighthouse implementation PR#10604 available for CL teams to assess complexity
- Csaba: preparing PR to clarify EIP-8411 chunking descriptor and Reed-Solomon scheme

organizational:

items.title: PQ-CL Breakout #2 (2026-11-18)
items.summary:
PQ-CL Breakout #2 - November 18, 2026

pq gasper aggregation bottleneck:
- 16-to-1 recursion takes 5s on $1,200 NUC hardware; 15s on cloud VPS — makes same-slot inclusion infeasible
- Delayed inclusion agreed as path forward: proposer includes attestations from 2 slots prior, removing recursion from hot path
- Best-aggregate propagation rule reverted; Potuz proposed staggered aggregator send times with self-censorship if not substantially better

pq gasper vs pqdc:
- PQDC advantage: head votes from ~500-validator committee need no aggregation; attestations move off critical path entirely
- Goal: finish PQ Gasper spec + vibe-code clients to validate feasibility; if aggregation proves untenable, move fully to PQDC

pq fork transition:
- Unregistered validators immediately exited at PQ fork with 16,384-epoch (~72 day) withdrawal delay for social-slash window
- MAX_COMMITTEES_PER_SLOT reduced 64→16 to match ATTESTATION_SUBNET_COUNT; max validators per committee to be 4×'d
- Restricting PQ key registration to 0x02 validators supported; encourages consolidation; EIP-8148 (CFI) likely needed for Hegota

devnet planning:
- First devnet: PQ Genesis only (no fork transition), no BLS validators; Barnabas to build Kurtosis tooling + pre-generate XMSS keys to S3
- Spec targeting ~3 hours post-call; devnet target by Monday; live launch demo planned for Friday's PQCL Breakout call

networking methodology:
- Csaba/Kamil to write methodology doc: simulations for parameter-space exploration; small devnets for implementation realism; large-scale not needed
- Kamil running daily simulations; next task: measure bandwidth gain from large-message broadcast optimizations for 200 KB subnet proofs

액션 아이템:
- Finish PQ Gasper spec with delayed attestation inclusion; share commit on PQCL channel
- Write networking methodology doc: rationale for simulation vs. devnet approach
- Benchmark LeanVM: 4 cores aggregation alongside 4 cores EL block execution; publish results

items.title:
New post on Eth Research!

EIP-8288: the networking side of recursive aggregatio
items.summary:
New post on Eth Research!

EIP-8288: the networking side of recursive aggregation

By:
- cskiraly
- Csaba Kiraly

🔗 https://t.co/bOzKTYAOWk

Highlights:
- Post-quantum signatures by themselves don’t necessarily break today’s mempool networking: simulations at ~15 signature tx/s show nodes can propagate/fetch them with modest upload (about one copy per tx per node), while one builder can still include everything.
- Recursive aggregation can also handle today’s signature-only load, but naïvely “pushing” a fresh proof to every peer every interval creates a large standing bandwidth cost that depends mostly on peer count (roughly peers × proof_size ÷ interval), even at low transaction rates.
- Switching from proof-push to ‘announce coverage then fetch proofs on demand’ can significantly reduce upload (especially at low load), but requires richer metadata and clear rules for when a node should fetch proofs—open questions for EIP-8437’s wire protocol.
- Who aggregates is crucial for privacy-transaction capacity: if only a fraction of nodes aggregate, the design of raw-transaction relay/fetch timeouts and whether nodes wait for covering proofs can swing capacity from very low to very high (in the study, ~6 to ≥72 privacy tx/s under different designs).
- The 1,000 ms aggregation interval only works if the assumed prover is fast enough: merging a node’s proof with peers’ proofs can consume most/all of the interval, and slower hardware can fail badly under privacy load—so EIP-8288 should specify the target prover/assumptions and what slower nodes should do.

ELI5:
Imagine Ethereum transactions sometimes come with very big “receipts” (signatures or privacy proofs). Instead of every computer on the network checking and passing around those big receipts one-by-one, EIP-8288 lets computers bundle many receipts together into one bigger but more efficient “super-receipt” (a recursive STARK proof). Then blocks only need to carry and verify the super-receipt. This turns the mempool into a network that not only shares transactions, but also continuously builds proofs. The article uses simulations to show that whether this works well depends heavily on networking rules (who sends proofs to whom, when peers download them, and how fast computers can build/merge proofs).

Very much agree with this. A few thoughts:
- We always always always underestimate the compounding complexity of interacting features. At the end of the day safely shipping something is quite dependent on a handful of people deeply thinking about these interactions.
- a PQ chain is useless if it breaks from much more mundane attack vectors. People not working on PQ will have plenty to do on that front. Focus on hardening has never had such high returns as right now, while the web as we know it is under assault
- Our goal should indeed be to ship features safely *and fast*, but I don't think this is in contradiction with a singular focus on PQ right now. We're going to move fastest when all of the smartest and most knowledgeable people in Ethereum R&D are pointing in the same direction, iterating fast together. We all know this to be true. This is what the Merge was! It was an incredible feat of coordination, engineering and testing, and took a little over a year even with what's basically primitive testing infrastructure compared to what we have now (shadow forks had to be invented!), and no AI.

items.title: Quick take from my side after reading the recent posts from @potuz_eth, @ethlabs
items.summary:
Quick take from my side after reading the recent posts from @potuz_eth, @ethlabs_org, @mikeneuder and @soispoke on PQAI. Definitely recommend reading all of them. Links below.

Very short summary: Potuz and Ethlabs want to go all in on PQ and only ship what's really needed. Mike thinks rushing PQ is premature, but agrees that hardening the clients is super important. Thomas wants to parallelise and keep shipping non-PQ features like FOCIL.

I think pqai will come with all kinds of threats, and AI getting better at finding bugs is the one we already experience. The PQ changes alone are already a lot of new code: new signatures, leanVM, much bigger messages on the p2p layer, new key handling. Every line of that needs to be understood by someone, tested and hardened. That's risky enough already, so I'd rather not add more features on top.

For people hunting bugs, it makes a big difference whether a fork is Frames or Frames + FOCIL. More code means more to understand and test, more interactions, and that doesn't really parallelise. So I could see the PQ work being done as "slim" feature forks (Frames, leanVM, DC), with FOCIL coming back once we know what PQ consensus looks like.

The only things I'd ship alongside are hardening and simplifications.
I think in times where AI gets crazy good at breaking things, that kind of work will be very welcome.

items.summary: This thread is for discussion of a draft ERC: Onchain Announcements . Summary. An announcement is a bracket: an Announcement event opens it, zero or more self-targeted calls execute atomically inside it, and an EndAnnouncement event closes it. items.title: One benefit of younger generations investing more in stonks and other digital th
items.summary:
One benefit of younger generations investing more in stonks and other digital things instead of housing is that it reduces perverse incentives that drive people to push to keep housing expensive, instead of rejoicing when prices drop as we do for all other life necessities.

That said, an advantage housing has/had is that it's a culture and policy-encouraged default of investing in a safe non-crazy thing that you can't easily liquidate. Modern platforms encourage the opposite of this, leading to more irresponsible behavior. We need the equivalent of those good properties that housing investment has, for modern digital assets.
 https://t.co/4uV8Q1rGuN

items.summary:
Bringing Aave App to Android and Tron marks an important strategic milestone for the Aave team.

Android accounts for roughly 72% of global mobile usage, with an even higher share in regions where access to financial opportunities remains limited.

Tron, meanwhile, has a significant user base across Latin America, Africa, and Asia, with nearly $100 billion in stablecoin supply, much of which is not earning yield.

Building a beautiful, intuitive, and delightful financial app on Android is no small feat, and our team has done an incredible job bringing this experience to life.

Aave's mission is to bring DeFi to everyone.

items.title:
New EIP!

Dependency frames for leanSPHINCS signatures

🔗 https://t.co/Pi0QkUUB
items.summary:
New EIP!

Dependency frames for leanSPHINCS signatures

🔗 https://t.co/Pi0QkUUBIK

Highlights:
- Adds a new EIP-8141 frame mode: a dependency verification frame that executes no EVM code and only declares required signature dependencies as (scheme, data_hash, verification_key_hash) triples.
- Defines only one dependency scheme initially: leanSPHINCS (stateless, Keccak-256-based, post-quantum), where a zero data_hash can mean “the transaction’s own signature hash.”
- Signatures are explicitly not included in the transaction encoding; they travel beside transactions in the mempool and blocks, and blocks include one signature per distinct dependency used by their transactions.
- All nodes verify these signatures outside the EVM (and can do so in parallel with execution); mempool nodes can reject transactions missing required signatures before simulation.
- The block header commits to the carried signatures, enabling a future upgrade to replace per-signature witnesses with a single aggregate proof (e.g., like EIP-8288) without changing transaction hashes or smart account logic for reading dependencies.

ELI5:
This proposal lets a transaction list which big post-quantum signatures it needs without stuffing those huge signatures inside the transaction itself. Instead, the signatures are carried next to the transactions in the block/mempool, verified by nodes outside the EVM, and smart accounts can read the list of required signatures from a special “frame” field.

items.title: Frame Transaction Breakout #8 (2026-11-17)
items.summary:
Frame Transaction Breakout #8 - Nov 17, 2026

eip8288 forward compatibility:
- EIP-8288 (signature and proof aggregation): frames must be forward-compatible; primary change is removing the signature list in favor of a PROOF frame mode
- Goal: users should not need to change wallets again when aggregation (EIP-8288) ships; forward-compat design is the priority over incremental devnet updates
- lightclient's sketch: new PROOF frame mode where initial content is a regular signature; protocol interprets it per 8288 shape in future forks

pq signatures and sphincs:
- PQ sigs without aggregation: even several hundred PQ sigs/block is only a few MB; aggregation is for efficiency, not security — don't block shipping

items.summary:
PQ-CL Breakout #1 - November 17, 2026

pq fork design:
- Pre-registration (EIP-8205-derived): free-of-charge validator key reservation before deposit; prevents race condition without requiring 1 ETH upfront
- PQ pre-registration spec PR built on Heze; author offered to rebase on Glamsterdam, which today's material already targets (preference stated at Devcon)
- BLS validators unregistered at fork: immediately exited but withdrawal delayed ~8,000 epochs; slashing handled via social consensus only

- Proposal: reduce committees 64→16 (matching subnets); each committee ~4× larger; aggregation cost estimated 2–2.5s to do a 16→1 recursion
- 64 proofs on global topic (~6.25 MiB/slot) identified as primary bandwidth concern; no clean solution reached; flagged as main open blocker
- Direction of travel floated as the first thing to try: 16 subnets / 16 committees / 4 aggregators per committee via RANDAO + balance-weighted look-ahead in beacon state; not settled
- If aggregation timing proves infeasible, preference is to skip long-slot workaround and move directly to Decoupled Consensus (DC)

proof of possession:
- XMSS proof of possession verified on EL side only (not stored on-chain); estimated gas cost small (~20–45k); no CL changes needed
- Decision: pre-registration authorized by withdrawal credentials only; operator/validator private key signing explicitly rejected

client implementation status:
- Lodestar: LeanVM bindings tested; disposable prototype code exists. ethlambda: LeanVM bindings tested + EIP-8483 on Heze; will rebase on Glamsterdam. Prysm: XMSS signing assembly planned; STARK side TBD

items.title: Discussions around light clients surface quite fundamental questions about the f
items.summary:
Discussions around light clients surface quite fundamental questions about the future of state exchange: With growing state, who'll be able to maintain it at an increasing cost, and what role do light clients play in the network.
Today, every full node helps its peers during sync and delivers them state (key -> value pairs), and a proof (MPT proof against the state root in the block header). MPT proofs can be quite big but it's still quite efficient for downloading large chunks of state e.g. during initial sync where the proof size is less of a problem relative to the total amount of data downloaded.
With Validity-Only-Partial-Statefulness (VOPS), Ethereum can recognize a low-hardware node that drops most of the EL state but keeps enough to still participate in the mempool, as a validator or an inclusion list builder. Such nodes are a great compromise for some use cases but have downstream effects: with today's state tree, those nodes cannot help others syncing anymore.

Syncing requires nodes to deliver a proof against the state root, and nodes who drop even tiny pieces of state risk not being able to compute those proofs. They become useless peers during sync.

It's an acceptable trade-off for some nodes, but the final design must ensure that it's incentive compatible (or at least maintains the status quo) to run a node that automatically contributes back to the network.
For that to work efficiently, we need a new tree (eip-8297), allowing nodes to drop state while still being able to deliver proofs to peers that ask for state they have. This allows VOPS nodes to sync other VOPS nodes, but doesn't answer the more challenging question of what to do with the rest of the state, and who keeps it.

- Delays in audits and outreach caused by EF reorgs and budget cuts; Marius accepts responsibility

- Affected protocols signaling willingness to fix indicate a January Glamsterdam date is acceptable

items.summary:
Post Quantum Transaction Signature (PQTS) Breakout #17 - October 28, 2026

testnet update:
- Testnet v03 launched on Daisugi (with Nethermind): single tx with STARK proof of 20 SPHINCS signatures under EIP-8288
- Post-DevCon testnet planned with EthPandaOps spam tooling for better benchmarks

sphincs parameter proposals:
- sphincs.art tool presented: explores SPHINCS parameter trade-offs (lifetime, shape, hash, FTS type) for Lean SPHINCS
- Default lifetime on sphincs.art is 2^30 (~1B signatures); reducing to 2^24 cuts size but raises key-rotation frequency
- Pruning improves keygen speed but leaks privacy after ~75 signatures; partial fix requires semi-trusted state, yields ~2,000 private sigs on Ledger
- Forest-of-WOTS FTS (Jonas Nick's sig.golf submission, Blockstream) gives >30% signing speedup but is novel, less MPC-friendly, and needs standard-model security proof
- Project 11 proposes two parameter sets: both use WOTS/WOTS+C, CAIC hash, lifetime 2^24; optimized for hardware wallets and MPC (SPHINCS G variant)

lifetime and key rotation debate:
- Bitcoin SPHINCS (Shrinks) currently at 2^40; Mikhail Kridinov open to lower values; Justin Drake advocates cross-chain alignment
- Circle hot wallets sign 30K–70K tx/day (~2^16–2^17); at 2^24 lifetime that is ~1.5 years before rotation
- Nico: surveyed 5 major exchanges — all said key rotation is trivially automatable; anything above 2^22–2^23 is sufficient
- Justin Drake argues for higher lifetime (2^30): easier UX communication, alignment with Bitcoin/Zcash, and room to reduce later
- Chat note: Bitcoin 2^40 accounts for off-chain protocols (e.g., high-volume Lightning nodes), not just on-chain use

mpc and hardware wallet constraints:
- WOTS forest is structurally worse for MPC (nearly 100% secret hashes vs ~50% for FORS); not just a compute-power problem
- Project 11: going from 2^24 to 2^32 is a make-or-break difference at the MPC layer, and rules out fast SPHINCS-G signing on a Ledger Nano S
- Justin Drake: proof-of-grinding via SNARK (host offloads grinding to laptop, proves correctness) expected to improve ~10x in ~12 months

액션 아이템:
- Circle (Daniel) to report internally on key-rotation feasibility and return with findings next call
- Emile to add 2^24 lifetime toggle to sphincs.art so parameter sets can be compared directly

P2P networking #10 - October 21, 2026

client updates:
- Lighthouse enabled partial data columns on mainnet by default in Monday's release
- Csaba: implemented message validation in go-libp2p at multiple levels; slides forthcoming next call
- Geth blsync CL light client updated to be Glamsterdam-compatible with efficiency improvements

snap enr discussions:
- Cross-client ENR analysis: Geth alone publishes a 'snap' key (empty array); no other clients set it; no EIP guidance on value or versioning
- Three options proposed: omit snap from ENR entirely; include with supported version; or keep as empty array (Geth current behavior)
- Edge cases: Reth skips SNAP 1, will support SNAP 2 in Glamsterdam; Nimbus EL can sync but not serve snap data

decoupled consensus simulation:
- Sukun presented decoupled consensus simulations (Cambridge workshop): decouple LMD-GHOST head vote (Goldfish) from FFG finality vote (Simplex); targets 4x faster finality
- Simulation: 500 cloud Prysm-fork nodes, 64 subnets, 2,500 validators/subnet (~25% above mainnet); Scenario 1 (staggered FFG) works but home nodes hit ~40 Mbps peak vs 25 Mbps limit
- EIP-8334 (bundle attestations): batching 4 votes reduces 960 bytes → 552 bytes; with partial messages, home node bandwidth drops well below 25 Mbps limit and Goldfish votes are >20% faster at P99
- Scenario 3 (3 committees/subnet, fully decoupled finality): works but Goldfish propagation degrades to ~1.2s without topic prioritization; topic priority work (Csaba) could resolve this
- Open design question: staggered publishing (Scenario 1) vs. multiple committees per subnet (Scenario 3); need to define desired properties before choosing

informed diffusion zcast:
- Csaba introduced zcast: fast & lean broadcast protocol built on segmentation, erasure coding, controlled I-have/I-want, and sampling; targets payloads and sampled broadcast, drawing its sampling ideas from FullDAS
- Benchmark: gossipsub today is far from optimal; zcast achieves sub-700 ms payload propagation with <2x bandwidth overhead even with 50 Mbps home builder uplink
- zcast is not designed for attestation aggregation (many-to-one / in-network compute); that remains a separate protocol domain
- Implementation: Go on top of go-libp2p/GossipSub + Python executable spec + formal modelling and verification (in progress); runs on Shadow and native QUIC; post on ethresear.ch with full technique breakdown
- Byzantine resilience tested up to 50% withholders and active malicious nodes; formal verification work ongoing to close remaining gaps

액션 아이템:
- Raise snap ENR behavior with Geth team; gather consensus on whether to include snap key and how to value it
- Share decoupled consensus simulation slides publicly for broader review

items.summary:
P2P networking #8 - September 09, 2026

client updates:
- Prysm: partial columns PR for Gloas fully reviewed/tested, awaiting one upstream PR before merge to release branch
- Prysm: peer scoring overhaul dev-complete; tested on Hoodi for one week, no regressions; adds per-agent observability and pruning metrics
- Lighthouse: fixing incorrectly ordered fields in partial messages; Gloas column gossip limit replacing static 8MB cap with dynamic limit based on blob schedule max
- Nethermind: sparse blob pool in master; working on IPv6 support, near completion

rowdas proposal:
- RowDAS adds row-based reconstruction duties to PeerDAS: vertical (distributed CPU across supernodes) and horizontal (supernodeless fallback) reconstruction
- Each supernode assigned a row duty (no custody requirement); duty-sharded variant skips row topics entirely, using only column topics — simpler first-stage option
- KZG reconstruction per blob ~162ms single-core; RowDAS reduces per-node CPU ~2 orders of magnitude; degrades to PeerDAS levels under adversarial conditions
- Implemented on Csaba's Prysm branch (on top of partial messages); row-based reconstruction without supernodes confirmed working at 65+ nodes

fast payload broadcast:
- 1MB payload over 50 Mbit uplink nodes (min-spec): current gossip-sub delivers last node in ~5s; all segmentation variants (A/B/C) converge near ~1s
- Variant A (normal gossip-sub + 32KB segments): 1.7s → 1.0s with batch publishing → further gains with phase-aware forwarding and disciplined pull (one requester per segment)
- Merkle commitment in the bid required to authenticate segments without full block; enables immediate per-segment forwarding upon receipt of signed beacon block
- ethp2p broadcast already implements chunking, push→pull phase transition, and pluggable nil encoder; Raúl offers to onboard collaborators and align with Csaba's work

eip proposals hegota:
- EIP-8411 (fast payload broadcast): replaces execution-payload topic with execution-payload-chunks; 64 segments, Merkle inclusion proof per chunk, payload-chunks-root added to bid; no erasure coding in v1 for simplicity
- EIP-8411 requires consensus change (bid field extension); without it, mixed-mode operation is possible but increases attack surface and buffering burden

ethp2p progress:
- Raúl implementing shared QUIC transport for Prysm: single endpoint serves both libp2p and ethp2p streams; stream routing via ALPN negotiation + first-byte slash detection; backwards-compatible with libp2p-only peers
- ethp2p payload broadcast branch hooked into Glamsterdam in Prysm; ready for DevNet testing
- Raúl previewed unified Ethereum networking specs site aggregating consensus-specs, EIPs, and ethp2p/Waggle specs in one taxonomy; unreleased, targeting this week
- ethp2p advantages over libp2p: unidirectional streams, datagrams, zero-RTT, session resumption, per-chunk stream interruption, slot-scoped cache lifetimes; lambdaclass has WIP Rust implementation

액션 아이템:
- Csaba to document partial-messages changes one-by-one for cross-team review and Waggle/ethp2p alignment
- Csaba and Raúl to align benchmarks and share code between simulation frameworks (Plisma vs ethp2p)
- Kamil to extend EIP-8411 with chunk-before-bid handling rules and payload-chunks-root field

items.title: Post Quantum Transaction Signatures #14 (2026-09-02)
items.summary:
Post Quantum Transaction Signature (PQTS) Breakout #14 - September 2, 2026

sphincs parameter overview:
- Lean SPHINCS chosen as PQ replacement for ECDSA; no cryptographic precompiles will be shipped; aligns with hash-based consensus/DA layer direction
- Moving away from Poseidon toward Blake/SHA via new 'Flock' system on Banner Fields; specific hash function TBD
- NIST April 2026 SPHINCS variant cuts signature from ~8KB to ~4KB but requires 1.45B hashes to sign — impractical for hardware wallets
- SPHINCS Minus C12 targets 2^14 signature budget (covers 99.99% of mainnet addresses); signing cost 37K hashes vs. 1.45B; still 47.5s on Ledger Nano S
- Riva Labs achieved 1.5s signing on Ledger Nano S Plus (2^24 budget) via offline precomputation of public values + grinding; paper forthcoming

pq1 hardware wallet demo:
- Freedom Factory PQ1 wallet: STM32U585 (Cortex-M33) + NXPSE050 secure element; XOR key split via TrustZone; SPHINCS Minus C10
- On-chip signing: ~1.1s; cold boot (with key derivation): ~3s; SHA-256 hardware accelerator on STM32 aids performance
- First EVT hardware received; all code open source (WIP); STM32U585 eval board ~$100 total to run today
- Targeting Q4 2026 consumer device availability; uses account abstraction (modified base smart account), not native ECDSA replacement
- Verification contract in Trail of Bits audit; exploring Lean/eCrypt formal verification via Rust-to-Lean toolchain

mldsa evm optimization:
- Fireblocks (Oren): MLDSA-44 EVM verification reduced from ~8M gas to 1.2M gas (6× improvement); FIPS-compliant, open source, research quality
- Key registration (one-time expanded key stored on-chain, ~20KB) costs ~4M gas; full cold verification ~9M gas unoptimized
- Main savings: eliminating quadratic memory expansion (~2M gas saved), 256-bit batched lane operations, Yul/assembly rewrites; ~10% further reduction possible
- At current gas prices, 1.2M gas verification costs ~$0.22; contract to be published same day or next
- Result supports community position against MLDSA precompile for Hegota; pure EVM sufficient at this gas cost

액션 아이템:
- Publish optimized MLDSA-44 EVM verification contract to announced repository
- Share Lean/eCrypt formal verification progress for SPHINCS firmware with community

- Nethermind: IPv6 support improvements; sparse blob pool merging to master soon; boot node release targeting next Nethermind release

research gossipsub dog liveness:
- DOG protocol: adversary with one physical node can disable all forwarding routes network-wide; even without adversary, counterexample shows connectivity not guaranteed
- GossipSub: under geometric latency model, ~100 adversary nodes with 80% latency advantage can separate ~40% of nodes; 99% of links vulnerable to targeted removal
- GossipSub outbound quota: adversary with 1% of identity pool can eventually take over both outbound mesh slots; iterative attack boosts separation rate further
- Latency advantage achievable by skipping signature validation or using direct fibre/low-latency network — wire protocol-compliant but behaviourally distinct
- Proposed mitigations: statistical delivery-latency feedback loops; self-health evaluation; attestation on-chain landing rate as outbound mesh quality signal; 'secret buddy' baseline comparison node

액션 아이템:
- Share Prysm peer scoring design doc with P2P working group before next call
- Share fast block diffusion design write-up with interested parties on request
- Publish document summarising AI-audit security issues including peer-forced blob recomputation

items.title: Frame Transaction Breakout #2 (2026-08-25)
items.summary:
Frame Transaction Breakout #2 - August 25, 2026

eip8141 frames status:
- EIP-8141 CFI'd for Hegota; devnet-zero in progress; question is whether to elevate to headliner
- Recent 8141 changes: Glamsterdam integration (2D gas, state gas as explicit second dimension), spec clarifications; signature list unchanged since May
- ethrex has two live testnets: privacy-only (Frames + FOCIL + recent roots) and Hegota-like playground (post-tx assertions, native UTXOs)

eip8130 proposal:
- EIP-8130 launching on Base (late September); OP Stack and Arbitrum also committing; decoupled authenticator-based account model
- 8130 thesis: no capability gap vs. 8141, but lower cost; 8141's coupled account model is the core objection
- Key 8130 advantage: authenticator declared top-level in tx — dependencies inspectable without tracing; enables permissionless payer innovation
- Conceded 8130 gap: cannot support post-execution gas payment (e.g., pay with ETH acquired during execution); 8141 supports this

technical debate:
- Felix (Geth): pure-function authenticators reduce DOS risk, but recent roots requires storage and cannot be truly pure
- Nicolas (cryptography): 8141 STARK aggregation of hash-based sigs is the L1 scaling path; enshrined 8130 authenticator set creates permanent governance burden as PQ landscape shifts
- Tsahi (Offchain Labs): 8130 authenticator-as-contract-address avoids coordination overhead for new signature schemes; wants 8141 to adopt this extensibility

convergence discussion:
- Nethermind: L1 should not enshrine any specific account model; generic primitives preferred, adapters choose their model
- lightclient: no client team supports 8130 as-is on L1; proposal to draft a companion EIP adding keystore to 8141 as the path forward
- Felix (Geth): keystore companion EIP for 8141 could enable account portability and satisfy L2 interop without enshrining full 8130 actor model

액션 아이템:
- Draft companion EIP adding keystore concept to EIP-8141 for cross-team review
- Base/8130 team to sync with L1 core devs before shipping 8130; commit to collab window before September fork
